Implants can replace single or multiple missing teeth with a natural look and strong bite, provided your gums and jawbone are healthy. We’ll review your medical history, 3D imaging, and habits (like smoking) to confirm candidacy. Helps prevent bone loss and shifting of nearby teeth. High long-term success with good home care and checkups. May require bone graft or sinus lift in low-bone areas. AAOMS — Dental Implants NIDCR — Dental Implants What’s the difference between traditional dentures and implant-supported dentures? Traditional dentures rest on the gums, while implant-supported options “snap” to dental implants for stability. Many patients report better chewing, speech, and comfort with fewer sore spots. Lower dentures benefit most from implant retention. Removable (snap-in) vs. fixed (screw-retained “All-on-X”). Still requires regular cleanings and maintenance. ADA MouthHealthy — Dentures NCBI — Implant Overdentures (overview) How long do crowns and bridges last? With proper home care and regular visits, many crowns and bridges last 10–15 years or longer. Nightguards, good flossing under bridges, and avoiding very hard foods can extend their lifespan. Porcelain, zirconia, and metal options to fit needs. Address clenching/grinding to reduce fracture risk. Routine x-rays help monitor margins and decay risk. ADA — Dental Crowns ADA — Dental Bridges Is professional teeth whitening safe, and will it work for me? When supervised by a dentist, whitening is considered safe and effective for natural enamel. It won’t lighten crowns, veneers, or fillings, and we’ll screen for causes of discoloration first. Short-term sensitivity is common and manageable. Custom trays help maintain results with less gum irritation. Avoid strong pigments (coffee/wine) for 24–48 hours after. ADA — Teeth Whitening FDA — Teeth Whitening Do you offer same-day or ceramic restorations? Many practices use digital scanners and in-office milling to deliver strong, tooth-colored restorations in one visit. Candidates are selected based on tooth structure, bite, and fracture risk. No messy impressions; faster turnaround. Precise fit from CAD/CAM workflows. Nightguard recommended for heavy grinders. ADA — Evidence-Based Dentistry Cochrane — Ceramic restorations (evidence) What options do you have for dental anxiety or sensitive gag reflex? We tailor comfort with calming communication, numbing gels, nitrous oxide (“laughing gas”), and—when appropriate—oral conscious or IV sedation. Your medical history and medications guide safe choices. Nitrous wears off quickly; you can usually drive yourself. Oral/IV sedation requires an escort and pre-op fasting. We screen for sleep apnea, heart, or respiratory issues. ADA — Sedation ADA Science & Research What does recovery look like after extractions or implant surgery? Most patients experience mild swelling and soreness for 2–3 days; stitches are often removed in about a week. Implants typically need a few months to fuse (osseointegrate) before final teeth are attached. Cold compresses and head elevation help with swelling. Soft diet; avoid straws/smoking to protect healing sites. Call us for increasing pain, fever, or unusual bleeding.
